title: Electrical Noise Produced by Micron-Sized Particles above a Surface Paul Trap
authors: Ben Saarel, Ozgur Sahin, Hartmut Häffner, Alpha T. N'Diaye
abstract: Electric field noise produced by the surface of ion trap electrodes reduces the fidelity of quantum computing operations. Despite decades of investigation its microscopic origins remain unclear. Here, we measure electric field noise at trapping locations along the symmetry axis of a linear surface Paul trap. We find that noise levels vary by three orders-of-magnitude in one 600$\,μ$m section of the trap. Optical and scanning electron microscope images show micron-sized particles close to the trapping locations with the highest noise levels. We find that modeling the particles as a lossy dielectric with a effective loss tangent $\tanθ=0.33(0.06)$ describes the magnitude of the noise, as well as its spatial and frequency dependence. Our observations may explain the large variation of reported noise levels in literature.
summary: The researchers investigated electric field noise limiting quantum operations in a surface Paul trap. They found that the noise is strongly correlated with micron-sized particles on the electrode surface. By modeling these particles as lossy dielectrics, they successfully explained the magnitude and frequency dependence of the measured noise, offering a key insight into improving ion trap fidelity.
main_problem: Electric field noise originating from the surface of ion trap electrodes degrades the fidelity of quantum computing operations, but its microscopic origins are unclear.
main_result: The measured electric field noise correlates strongly with the presence of micron-sized particles on the trap surface, and this noise can be successfully modeled by treating these particles as lossy dielectrics.
method: The authors measured the heating rate ($\dot{n}$) of a single trapped ion's motion to quantify the spectral density of electric field noise ($S_E(\omega)$).
model_or_system: The experiment uses a linear surface Paul trap. The theoretical model treats the noise source as dielectric particles on the electrode surface, whose dissipation is governed by an effective loss tangent ($	an	heta$).
key_observables: Electric field noise levels (measured via ion heating rate $\dot{n}$), frequency dependence of noise ($S_E(\omega) \propto 1/\omega$), and particle presence visualized via SEM/CCD.
important_parameters: The effective loss tangent was determined to be $	an	heta = 0.33(0.06)$. Noise levels varied by three orders-of-magnitude across a $600\,\mu	ext{m}$ section.
main_assumptions: Particles are modeled as lossy dielectrics, and low-noise regions are assumed to be limited by mechanisms similar to other low-noise traps.
figures_summary: Figures show trap fabrication details, measured heating rates across different locations (L1-L7), frequency dependence fits for selected sites, and microscopy images confirming particle presence near high-noise areas.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of noise in ion traps, presents measurements showing strong spatial variation correlated with particles, develops a theoretical model linking this noise to dielectric loss, and validates the model against measured frequency and spatial dependencies.
why_interesting: This work provides crucial experimental grounding for open quantum system modeling in trapped ions. By quantifying environmental noise sources (surface defects) using established electromagnetic theory, it helps refine decoherence models essential for scaling up ion-trap quantum computers.

Fig. 2 displays the measured heating rates for ω = 2π × 1 MHz at various trapping locations along the length of the trap. For positions L1-L3, the heating rates remain constant at ≈200quanta/s. For positions L3-L7, the heating rate depends strongly on the trapping location z. The maximum heating rate we measure is 77000(7000) quanta/s at location L6. Fig. 3 shows the scaling of the heating rate with motional frequency ω at selected locations along the trap.
